findings.text: PROGRAM_KEY_SUFFIX is defined and never read anywhere in the tree; the suffix that actually governs the count is cache_reuse_summary.py:16 MARKER_SUFFIX, which served_keys reads. The constant is a second definition of the one fact this node's repair set out to keep in one place, and it survives as documentation of a rule no code enforces.

build_receipt writes both "status" and "command_status" from the same argument, so the row it returns carries the command's status under the field name that means the row's own status everywhere else (main overwrites it at :103). A caller that used build_receipt directly, or a reader of a receipt written before :103 runs, sees a status that is not the row's outcome.

the repair's effect lives in main's wiring, which no test reaches: reverting :121 to 'return status', or deleting the record["status"] = program_status(...) assignment at :103, restores the original defect and leaves all seven cases in tests/test_cache_guard.py green, because the tests call program_status directly. The end-to-end evidence exists only as logs (repair-prewarm-status-tolerate.log / -strict.log), so a later regression of the wiring is unguarded.

test_served_directory_reports_program_key_entries takes the monkeypatch fixture and never uses it, calling jax.config.update("jax_compilation_cache_dir", ...) at :62 directly; the global then points at a tmp_path pytest deletes, so every later test in the same process that reads the guard's served directory (test_marker_begins_a_line_after_unterminated_output at :90 does, through emit_receipt) runs against a vanished directory and sees served_entries 0.

negative_control_log names arm-old-pin.log, whose three failing ids (test_the_accelerator_routes_agree_on_the_fixed_point and the two differentiability cases) are exactly the three the head arm arm-warm.log also fails, so this log shows no test the head does not fail. The two logs that do redden the new tests — negative-control-reverted-counter.log and negative-control-reverted-prewarm-status.log, each 1 failed with EXIT=1 — are listed only under test_logs, so the single field the admission check reads names the weaker control.

the landing line reports '4 passed at head against 4 failed at base' while repair-head.log and repair-base.log carry 7 passed and 7 failed, and the H200 arm that carries the zero-compile measure (arm-warm.log:2 REVISION=1efb2faa3) predates 82a36d80f, so that log's served_entries field was written by the counter 82a36d80f supersedes; the hits/misses/compile-seconds figures the measure rests on are unaffected, but the recorded arm is not the reviewed code.
